newsitem.title: USA: NASD to be examined for possible restructure- Zarb.
newsitem.headline: NASD to be examined for possible restructure- Zarb.

text.p: Frank Zarb, National Association of Securities Dealers' chief, said Monday he plans to look at all aspects of the self-regulatory group and its two subidiaries on ways it can be improved.

The "Reinvesting in our Future" campaign is geared toward taking an overall look at the internal structure of the organization with the intent of increasing its efficiency, Zarb told told reporters at an informal briefing.
NASD employes well over 2,000 people worldwide.

Zarb said, "The internal look may show it has been doing things that don't need to be done anymore, or will find things need to be done better, or more efficiently with fewer people, or find things that we should be doing that we're not doing."
He said the reexamination does not mean downsizing or layoffs. "If we do our jobs right, we're going to have more employees rather than fewer two or three years from now."
There is nothing sacred in the reinvention of the self-reulatory group, except their "grounding principles", Zarb said, but added there is hardly an area that is not going to see some improvement.
NASD, a trade group for the U.S. financial industry, runs the Nasdaq stock market as a separate unit, while NASDR is its regulatory arm.
Zarb also said he has proposed there be a look and review of the three-board structure of the NASD, Nasdaq and NASDR.
"Review the existing structure and take some measurements and make some intelligent decisions," Zarb said, adding "people do that in the real world all the time."
Everything from a much larger single board to modifying existing boards and everything in between is under consideration, Zarb said.
